method.rationale: Scope-preserving residual search: retain v003's inexpensive verification cascade, but make query-induced exclusions visible and use a bounded residual-coverage pass before stopping. Unlike a census anchor, source-bundle allocation, or cohort sampling, this targets silent narrowing of eligible subtypes and premature saturation. Parallel's observed 135 correct finds per dollar versus Exa's 56.8 supports retaining cheap probes, not assuming equivalent accuracy. The inspected incomplete attempt motivates the hypothesis but does not establish that it will recover its missing item.
method.instructions: Define X and Y exactly, including entity unit, exclusions, effective dates, eligible subtypes and group-membership rules. Start sequentially with one X-only search, one Y-only search and one conjunction search, using the user's broad predicate wording rather than a familiar subtype. Maintain deduplicated X/Y frontiers and an identity/evidence ledger. Also maintain a compact scope ledger: for each discovery query record added restrictions not required by the hunt (subtype, occupation, geography, era, source or familiar-name terms). A successful restricted query does not establish coverage of its parent category. Derive a few meaningful sibling partitions from source taxonomies or the eligibility definition; do not invent an exhaustive cross-product or enumerate a whole census by default. Run short discovery/check rounds, prioritizing expected verified additions per total resolution cost. Each round's neglected-subtype or reverse-frontier probe must address a specific untested scope-ledger cell or remove a recorded accidental restriction; merely paraphrasing a prior conjunction does not qualify. Check source-backed candidates on Parallel for only unresolved predicates, supplying identity and existing evidence. Use small affordable batches, price every candidate, and do not recheck established facts. No result means unresolved, not false; reject only on contradiction or an exhaustive applicable source. Escalate promising ambiguous or conflicting cases individually to Exa. After two discovery searches add no plausible identities, prohibit synonymous conjunction searches and perform a residual-scope pass: identify the most consequential restriction accumulated so far, try a sibling subtype or unrestricted parent on the opposite frontier, then resolve resulting candidates before further discovery. Reserve at least 35% of initial funds for evidence and stop discovery whenever pending checks require the remaining funds. Before submitting with spare funds, perform up to three affordable residual probes covering distinct untested restrictions or source partitions, retaining enough funds to verify their likely candidates. Stop this pass after two probes add neither candidates nor useful evidence; do not spend merely to exhaust the budget. Finish with identity, predicate, subtype and effective-date audits; submit supported intersections only and never infer completeness from saturation.
method.routing_rules: Parallel alone, default tier, 8 results for baseline and residual discovery, 4 for exact missing-fact checks. No routine also variants or broad auto-routing. Price candidate batches as the sum of queries and provider charges; fewer results are not presumed cheaper. Exa alone with 4 results for selected unresolved identities where ambiguity, conflicting evidence or inaccessibility warrants the higher cost. At most one initial Exa discovery probe after Parallel stagnation, continued only if it contributes useful new identities or evidence. Try a genuinely different scope partition on Parallel before buying provider diversity for a repetitive query. Authoritative-domain filters are for targeted evidence, not general frontier coverage; relax failed filters. Use publication-date filters only when publication date itself determines eligibility, and verify effective dates in content.
method.fetch_policy: Reuse cached source facts. Fetch authoritative pages that can settle missing identity or predicates, and useful multi-candidate lists, rather than every result. When a list is used for scope coverage, inspect its stated subtype, date range and pagination/section links; an excerpt or one section is not an exhausted category. Follow only sections tied to a promising uncovered partition, without committing to bulk census extraction. After a blocked or uninformative page, make one targeted alternate-source attempt rather than a fetch chain.

candidates.title: Enforced Discovery State Transitions
candidates.rationale: Make v007's largely advisory pivot rule executable through query admission and persistent cooldowns. The inspected 48-search attempt illustrates noncompliance rather than disproving the pivot hypothesis. Retain Parallel: observed attributed yield is 162.3 correct finds per dollar versus Exa's 84.5, not a controlled accuracy comparison. This candidate changes search scheduling, not the anchoring unit.
candidates.instructions:
Define X and Y, entity unit, exclusions, eligible subtypes, membership rules and effective dates. Sequentially run one unrestricted X-only search, one unrestricted Y-only search and one broad conjunction. Maintain deduplicated frontiers, an identity/evidence ledger and a scope ledger. Reserve at least 35% of initial funds for evidence; price all candidate queries and fetches before discovery.
Use explicit states: DISCOVER, RESOLVE, PIVOT, AUDIT. Before each discovery call write a compact action ticket: frontier; source-backed partition; added restrictions; genuinely new coverage expected; cost including likely checks. Reject a ticket that merely paraphrases an already tried conjunction or adds familiar names without a source-backed reason. Equivalent predicate/subtype/source combinations share one query-family ID, regardless of wording. Record new identities and useful evidence after each call.
In DISCOVER, permit at most two consecutive discovery calls before resolving promising pending identities. Select the next frontier by expected verified additions per total resolution cost. Check only unresolved predicates in small affordable Parallel batches, supplying identity and existing evidence. No result is unresolved, not rejection. Reject only on contradiction or an exhaustive applicable record. Escalate selected ambiguous or conflicting cases individually to Exa.
Two discovery calls yielding no plausible new identity force PIVOT. Freeze their query families for the rest of the hunt unless newly retrieved evidence changes the question. The next discovery action must be an X-only or Y-only source-backed sibling partition or unrestricted parent on the opposite frontier; it must omit the other predicate and remove a recorded restriction. Resolve resulting candidates before further discovery. If that pivot fails, try at most one distinct source partition or one permitted provider-diversity probe; do not return to frozen conjunctions. A genuinely new source or identity can reopen only its relevant family, not reset all counters.
Stop discovery when pending resolution costs consume remaining funds. Before submission, use up to three affordable residual probes for distinct untested restrictions, stopping after two with neither candidates nor useful evidence. Audit identity, both predicates, membership, subtype and dates. Submit supported intersections only; saturation is not completeness.
candidates.routing_rules: Parallel alone, default tier, 8 results for discovery and 4 for exact missing facts and check_candidates. No routine also variants or auto-routing. Charge each candidate and provider separately; result limits are not assumed to reduce prices. Exa alone, 4 results, for individual evidence conflicts or identity ambiguity. Allow at most one Exa discovery probe only after a genuinely different Parallel scope partition fails, continuing only on useful incremental identities or evidence. Use domain filters only for targeted source checks, relax failed filters, and use publication-date filters only when publication date determines eligibility.
candidates.fetch_policy: Reuse cached facts. Fetch authoritative pages settling missing facts or useful candidate lists. Record each list's scope, date, sections and pagination; never equate an excerpt with coverage. Fetch only sections justified by an action ticket. A blocked or uninformative fetch permits one targeted alternate source, not a chain. Include fetch costs in action tickets.

candidates.title: Bounded Record Join Search
candidates.rationale: Test a conditional record-level join instead of relying on search rankings to surface intersections. The full-recall 387787ee6f inspected list sections and checked source-backed identities, whereas 59f7c7f036 missed one despite speculative checks. This is a hypothesis, not proof that section fetching caused the gain. Unlike discarded census-first and source-bundle methods, this uses a capped pilot on either frontier, retains cheap verification, and abandons low-yield extraction early.
candidates.instructions:
Define X and Y exactly, including entity unit, exclusions, eligible subtypes, group membership and effective dates. Begin sequentially with broad X-only, Y-only and conjunction searches. Maintain deduplicated identity/evidence and scope ledgers. Reserve at least 35% of initial funds for resolution and price candidate checks individually.
Assess both frontiers for a finite, accessible source with explicit records proving one predicate. Choose the side with lower expected extraction plus missing-predicate verification cost, not simply fewer apparent members. Do not commit to a census. If neither side has usable records, use short adaptive dual-frontier discovery/check rounds with v007-style scope correction.
When a useful source exists, spend at most 10% of initial funds on a record-join pilot, including fetching and checks. Inspect the source's taxonomy, pagination, effective dates and actual returned extent. Select one small source-defined section with plausible overlap and one previously uninspected section not chosen for familiar names. Extract identities and existing predicate evidence from records, not search snippets alone. Check the missing predicate for at most three source-backed identities at a time, resolving those before extending the section. Record section position and unresolved records so partial inspection cannot masquerade as exhaustion. A record's abbreviated occupation or description is not a reason to reject it.
Continue record inspection only if the pilot supplies a verified addition or concrete evidence making another small batch competitive with ordinary discovery. If two consecutive batches add neither verified intersections nor useful evidence, suspend that source, retain unresolved identities, and switch frontier or discovery mode. Extension is always incremental; do not extract the entire catalog or buy checks for a large speculative queue. Within a chosen section, avoid repeatedly selecting only recognizable identities. At each extension compare total resolution cost with an untested sibling partition on the other frontier.
Use Parallel checks only for unresolved facts, supplying existing evidence and identity. Treat no result as unresolved and reject only on contradiction or an exhaustive applicable source. Escalate promising ambiguity or conflict individually to Exa. After two ordinary discovery searches yield no identities, prohibit synonymous conjunctions and use a distinct source section or a less restricted opposite-frontier probe. Stop discovery when pending checks need the remaining budget. With spare funds, inspect up to three distinct residual partitions, stopping after two fruitless probes and preserving verification funds. Finish with identity, predicate, membership, subtype and effective-date audits; submit only supported intersections without claiming completeness from partial source coverage.
candidates.routing_rules: Parallel alone, default tier, 8 results for source discovery and residual probes; 4 for exact unresolved facts and check_candidates. No routine also variants, auto-routing or bulk Exa checking. Budget each candidate separately and do not presume fewer results cost less. Exa alone with 4 results for selected ambiguous or conflicting identities; at most one initial discovery probe after a different Parallel partition has failed, continued only with useful incremental evidence. Authoritative-domain filters target record evidence, not general coverage; relax failed filters. Publication-date filters apply only to publication-date eligibility; verify effective dates in source content.
candidates.fetch_policy: Fetch a promising structured list or source section once, recording actual visible rows, section boundaries, filters, pagination and dates. Reuse all extracted facts. Follow a next-page or section link only within the capped pilot or an explicitly justified incremental extension. Prefer accessible record views over repeated fetches of truncated pages. Do not assume a requested large page size was honored. One targeted alternate-source attempt after a blocked or uninformative fetch; abandon extraction if still unusable. Fetch authoritative individual records to settle identity or unresolved predicates, not every search result.
